title: Engineering a 2.5D Urban Twin: Semantic GeoAI Discovery and Blockchain-Provenanced Updates
authors: Nicula A.-S.
source_title: 2026 International Conference on Frontiers of Engineering and Emerging Technologies, FET 2026
abstract: This work presents an urban digital twin for Timioara, Romania built from fragmented public datasets in the absence of official 3D city models. The implementation integrates municipal CKAN resources, OpenStreetMap extracts, and Copernicus elevation data through adapter-based ingestion with enforced schemas and automated versioning. Three technical challenges motivated the design: heterogeneous coordinate reference systems (Stereo 70, WGS84, UTM Zone 34N) requiring canonical reprojection, conflicting update cadences across daily OSM snapshots and static municipal layers, and inconsistent geometry validity requiring automated repair workflows. Vector embeddings enable semantic search over dataset metadata; Precision@5 improves from 0.46 to 0.74 compared to keyword approaches, with P95 query latency under 510ms. Blockchain Merkle roots anchor data provenance while keeping geospatial files off-chain; tamper detection achieved 100% accuracy across 400 deliberate corruption trials. Ten repeated builds achieved identical hashes with 98.5% resource retrieval success, completing in 46 minutes with 2.8% cryptographic overhead. The system generates a 2.5D representation pairing OSM building footprints with inferred heights from Copernicus DEM and building-level attributes. The results demonstrate that operational urban twins can be assembled from incomplete, multi-authority sources when paired with strict version control, semantic discovery, and cryptographic integrity verification, enabling municipal stakeholders to query integrated infrastructure data reliably. © 2026 IEEE.

title: Digital Twins and Artificial Intelligence for Sustainable Infrastructure Management: A Future Perspective
authors: Tanoli W.A.; Khan H.; Shahid U.; Mahmood Q.
source_title: 2026 International Conference on Frontiers of Engineering and Emerging Technologies, FET 2026
abstract: The convergence of digital twin (DT) technology and artificial intelligence (AI) represents a transformative advancement in sustainable infrastructure management. This paper synthesizes current research on DT-AI integration for infrastructure applications across urban planning, building operations, structural health monitoring, and environmental management. Through systematic review of 70 peer-reviewed publications spanning 2020 to 2026, key technological enablers including IoT sensor networks, machine learning algorithms, and edge computing platforms were identified. A taxonomic classification distinguishes data-driven approaches (60 percent) from physics-informed methods (17 percent) and hybrid implementations (23 percent), while architectural analysis compares centralized cloud-based systems with distributed edge computing deployments. The analysis reveals that AI-enhanced digital twins achieve energy optimization of 20 to 30 percent, predictive maintenance accuracy of 96 percent, and material recovery rates of 60 percent in circular economy applications. We propose a Sustainable Digital Twin Framework (SDTF) with detailed operational specifications for data acquisition, AI-based processing, decision support, and feedback control layers. Implementation challenges including data interoperability, cybersecurity vulnerabilities, and formal verification requirements are analyzed alongside emerging solutions. Research limitations and future directions are identified to guide continued advancement. © 2026 IEEE.

title: Designing maths-based STEAM activities for civil engineering curricula
authors: R. Chacón; M. R. Estela
source_title: 2020 IEEE Frontiers in Education Conference (FIE)
abstract: This work-in-progress innovative practice describes a set of pedagogical activities designed for students of 1st, 2nd and 3rd year of civil engineering programs. The pedagogical project has a twofold aim: i) infusing fabrication, coding and instrumentation in civil engineering courses and ii) fostering motivation and creativity among students by merging STEAM and Maths. For this purpose, a set of hands-on activities described herein encompasses concepts of calculus (functions, curves and derivatives), concepts of surveying (construction and measurement using sensors and microcontrollers by means of a fabrication of a low-cost Lidar) and concepts of algorithmic programming in which measurement and programming are blended together. Three workshops coupled with multimedia documents are prepared. Firstly, a workshop related to programming mathematical curves and derivatives in the coding platform Processing whose aim is to reinforce coding skills to our students. Secondly, a workshop related to the development of the Lidar using electronic prototyping boards such as Arduino whose aim is to introduce instrumentation skills to them. Thirdly, a workshop related to the use of algorithmic programming design platforms such as Grasshopper whose aim is to couple measurement and coding together. These activities are conceived for formal infusion in the next generation of civil engineering courses to be deployed at our school from 2020 onwards.

title: Reconstructing Historical Monuments and Environments: A Digital Approach to Education
authors: Casillo M.; Cecere L.; Colace F.; Lorusso A.; Pellegrino M.
source_title: Proceedings - Frontiers in Education Conference, FIE
abstract: The advancement of digital technologies is radically transforming the ways in which historical and architectural heritage is studied, preserved and passed on to future generations. This work proposes an integrated methodology for the digital reconstruction and management of historical monuments, based on the integrated use of Heritage Building Information Modeling (HBIM), Digital Twin (DT), IoT sensors and Machine Learning (ML) algorithms. Through the creation of high-fidelity digital models, updated in real time through environmental monitoring systems, it is possible to obtain a dynamic and predictive vision of the state of health of historical structures. The case study of the Leproso Bridge in Benevento, constitutes a concrete example of the application of this methodology: starting from surveys performed with terrestrial laser scanners and drone photogrammetry, an HBIM model was generated and subsequently integrated with data from environmental sensors, to develop a functional DT for the simulation of evolutionary scenarios, both historical and future. This digital platform makes it possible to visualise the transformations undergone by the artefact over time, monitor its current state, and predict structural degradation phenomena through automated analyses. In addition to its contribution in terms of conservation, the proposed approach represents an innovative educational resource. Students and teachers are involved in immersive, interdisciplinary learning experiences that combine art history, structural engineering, digital modelling and materials science. The interactive and data-driven environment fosters the development of transversal skills such as critical thinking, collaboration between disciplines and the conscious use of technology in heritage conservation. In conclusion, the combination of HBIM, DT, IoT and AI emerges as a powerful tool for both research and conservation design, as well as for historical memory education in a sustainable and participatory perspective © 2025 IEEE.

title: Digital Twin and Predictive Maintenance in Cultural Heritage: A Multidisciplinary Educational Experience with HBIM and IoT
authors: Colace F.; Ferrandino F.; Lombardi M.; Lorusso A.; Valentino C.
source_title: Proceedings - Frontiers in Education Conference, FIE
abstract: This Research to Practice Full Paper describes a project that combines different fields to include Heritage Building Information Modelling (HBIM), Internet of Things (IoT) sensor systems, and the digital twin (DT) concept into the hands-on learning experiences for construction engineering and architecture students at the university. This methodology was used in the 'Computer Graphics' course at the University of Salerno, where third-year students engaged in a data-driven digital workflow concerning the genuine case study of Villa Regina, a Roman rural villa situated inside the archaeological site of Pompeii. The students engaged thoroughly in the complete digitization process, encompassing 3D surveying through terrestrial laser scanning and aerial photogrammetry and culminating in the development of HBIM models augmented with semantic and degradation metadata. Subsequently, they developed and executed IoT-based monitoring systems utilizing Raspberry Pi and Arduino platforms and constructed DT simulations to investigate predictive maintenance tactics. An interdisciplinary collaboration between architecture, computer science, and conservation supported the course, which was structured on a project-based learning framework. The assessment, which was conducted through structured surveys and project analysis, demonstrated substantial improvements in technical proficiency, data literacy, and systems thinking. Despite their little prior experience, the students have effectively learned the fundamentals of sensor integration and real-time data processing and indicated greater enthusiasm for using smart technologies in cultural heritage contexts. The results demonstrate the usefulness of combining digital heritage methods with practical engineering training for large-scale teaching. Authentic, cross-disciplinary, and digitally-based learning experiences can be used in a variety of academic and cultural settings that want to change their program. © 2025 IEEE.

title: A Conceptual Framework for Neonatal Motor Activity Monitoring Using Digital Twin Technology and Computer Vision: A Preliminary Study
authors: Nakashima R.; Matsumoto H.; Zin T.T.; Kodama Y.
source_title: GCCE 2025 - 2025 IEEE 14th Global Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: Continuous non-contact monitoring of neonatal motor activity in the neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) is crucial for early detection of neurological disorders and for guiding timely clinical interventions. We introduce an infrared-driven skeleton-estimation prototype designed for real-time operation that generates a live virtual “digital twin” of the infant's posture to support clinician assessment. A deep-learning pose model was fine-tuned on a bespoke infrared key-point dataset, and three motion-quantification filters were evaluated: raw differencing (Method A), center-aligned suppression (Method B), and a newly proposed skeleton template-matching filter (Method C). Tests on a life-sized neonatal mannequin confirmed centimetric joint-localization accuracy, reliable detection of 50-pixel hand displacements, and reduction of simulated camera-shake artifacts to within five pixels. Building on these results, a follow-up evaluation on pre-term neonates showed that Method C suppressed static key-point noise by 78 % while preserving physiological motion. This combined mannequin and in-vivo evidence demonstrates the clinical feasibility of our infrared digital-twin framework and establishes a foundation for automated assessment of pre-term motor development. © 2025 IEEE.

abstract: Most existing digital twin (DT) frameworks for urban systems treat wireless networks as passive conduits, lacking adaptability to the application-level contexts. This poses challenges in intelligent transportation systems (ITS), where real-time wireless optimization is vital. We implemented a prototype using the Simulation of Urban Mobility (SUMO) traffic flow, 3D city models, and Sionna RT within Unreal Engine 5 (UE5), enabling synchronized mobility and wireless simulation. The WI-DT platform supports early stage exploration of vision-aided V2X communication in a unified cyber-physical environment.

title: Design and Research of Smart Sluice Station Based on GIS and BIM
authors: Z. Li; X. Liu; X. Yang
source_title: 2023 30th International Conference on Geoinformatics
abstract: As an important water conservancy facility, sluice plays an important role in water conveyance, flood control, drainage and navigation. At present, the management of the sluice station is mainly based on manual control and general two-dimensional information management system. However, most sluice stations are long project lines and lots of engineering points, which easily leads to many management problems such as high monitoring and maintenance costs and difficult policy coordination. To address this problem, this study combined BIM with GIS to develop an intelligent early warning and dispatching system. Based on the BIM model, three-dimensional (3D) city building model and remote sensing data, the proposed smart sluice station system integrated GIS, BIM and IoT technology, built a smart sluice station cloud platform, and realized the remote unified management system for sluice station. As a study case, the proposed system was applied to Cijiang Sluice Station, and the results show that the proposed system can realize remote monitoring, early warning and real-time scheduling of the sluice station, which has greatly saved time and costs for the sluice management.

abstract: Building Information Modeling (BIM) has primarily been applied to general construction projects, with limited attention to the unique requirements of electrical substations. This research addresses this gap by developing a substation BIM catalog with guidelines specifically for electrical substations, tailored to Latin America (Latam). This catalog emphasizes the importance of defining the Level of Information Need (LOIN) and integrates Lean Construction principles to prevent model overload and ensure efficient lifecycle management. Additionally, this paper explores the future of substation management through Digital Twins and Virtual Reality, maintaining the single source of truth principle and enhancing various BIM uses such as Asset Management and Preventive Maintenance Scheduling. This paper presents an overview of our substation catalog, shares experiences from Latam and Europe, and provides recommendations for effective BIM implementation in substation projects across the region.

The key contributions of this research work is to reduce the runtime for assigning work-buildings, using the following 3 strategies: A bounding-box heuristic for reducing runtime of our A∗ implementation; a ring-filter to reduce candidate work-buildings; and Using distributed computing (via MPI and OpenMP) with a custom load balancing approach. Collectively, these strategies enabled us to successfully generate models for large cities such as New York, Los Angeles, and Chicago in < 24 hours using 512 cores.  © 2025 IEEE.

title: Adaptive Environmental Control for Space Habitats Using Proximal Policy Optimization
authors: B. Tidke; S. Omkumar; S. P. Vimal; V. G. Sivakumar; M. R; T. R. GaneshBabu
source_title: 2025 9th International Conference on I-SMAC (IoT in Social, Mobile, Analytics and Cloud) (I-SMAC)
abstract: Longer space missions need autonomous systems that can sustain stable and secure living conditions inside confined habitats. Conventional control approaches, such as PID controllers, often have difficulties in adapting to dynamic environmental fluctuations and varying occupancy, hence constraining efficiency and responsiveness. This study presents an adaptive environmental management system using Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO), a reinforcement learning (RL) method, to control temperature, humidity, $\text{CO}_{2}$ concentrations, and air pressure. An advanced simulation environment was created to train the PPO agent, including authentic sensor functionalities and actuator limitations. A comparative assessment against PID control under fluctuating occupancy and equipment loads indicates that the PPO system sustained all environmental parameters within optimal thresholds 98.3% of the time, enhanced $\text{CO}_{2}$ regulation efficiency by 19.2%, decreased energy consumption by 22.5%, and reacted 37% more quickly to dynamic changes. The findings indicate that PPO enables intelligent, self-optimising environmental management with improved flexibility and energy efficiency. The proposed technology provides a scalable solution for life support in extraterrestrial habitats, establishing a crucial basis for viable expeditions to the Moon, Mars, and beyond.

title: Design and Application of Digital Protection Platform of Intangible Heritage Based on Virtual Reality Technology
authors: N. Lu; H. Jiang
source_title: 2025 2nd International Conference on Intelligent Algorithms for Computational Intelligence Systems (IACIS)
abstract: The preservation and exhibition of intangible cultural heritage (ICH) through traditional methods are often faced with the challenges of low interactivity, dispersed documentation, and static exhibitions that do not capture the immersive and experiential qualitative of cultural practices. These limitations hinder audience interaction and constrain the potential of such systems to transmit the dynamic and evolving nature of ICH. As a countermeasure to these hurdles, this research offers a Virtual Reality (VR) technology-based digital protection platform for ICH. VR presents an innovative solution by building interactive, three-dimensional environments where the people engage with cultural expressions like rituals, performances, crafts, and oral traditions in real time. The proposed system combines digital archiving, interactive narrative, and simulation mechanisms to bring increased accessibility and increased understanding of ICH. Comparative analysis with other traditional documentation processes and earlier digital methods shows that the VR-based platform enhances immersion, engagement, and retention of cultural knowledge significantly. Empirical findings depict greater satisfaction and understanding among users who go through VR-driven cultural simulations than in traditional methods. Though technical hurdles continue in content development and system tuning, the conclusions confirm the value of VR in preserving ICH and establish a forward-thinking framework for future digital preservation and learning uses.

title: Lightweight Visual Semantic Extraction and Real-Time Mapping for Engineering Digital Twins: An Edge–Cloud Collaborative Framework
authors: H. Chen; C. Liu; Y. Liu; S. Qiao; X. Chen; M. Li
source_title: 2025 7th International Academic Exchange Conference on Science and Technology Innovation (IAECST)
abstract: To tackle challenges such as limited network bandwidth, scarce edge computing resources, and high virtual-real interaction latency in engineering Digital Twin (DT) systems at construction sites, this paper proposes a cloud-edge collaborative visual-semantic processing mechanism. First, a collaborative computing architecture of "lightweight extraction at the edge, global mapping in the cloud" is constructed. At the edge, an improved LE-YOLO network is designed, which reconstructs the backbone with GhostNet modules and integrates the CBAM attention mechanism. On NVIDIA Jetson Nano devices, the network achieves real-time inference at 38.5 FPS while maintaining an mAP of 83.5%, reducing parameters by 34.4% compared with YOLOv8n. Second, a structured JSON-based semantic streaming protocol is designed to enable efficient edge–cloud communication. Based on this protocol, a visual–geometric fusion mapping algorithm is further proposed, in which a ray-casting strategy is employed to map 2D visual semantics onto 3D BIM models in real time, achieving accurate virtual–real spatial alignment. Experiments show that this mechanism saves 99.2% of bandwidth compared to traditional video streaming under weak network conditions, eliminates congestion and stuttering caused by video backhaul, and controls end-to-end latency within 100 ms, effectively enabling low-latency and high-consistency virtual–real synchronization for real-world construction site perception tasks.

title: FPGA-Based Digital Twin Implementation for Mechatronic System Monitoring
authors: Nwoke J.; Milanesi M.; Viola J.; Chen Y.Q.
source_title: 2023 5th International Conference on Industrial Artificial Intelligence, IAI 2023
abstract: Digital Twin is a driving technology for Industry 4.0 that enables novel capabilities like smart process control, fault detection, or remaining useful life estimation. Since a Digital Twin is an up-to-date representation of an actual physical process, building this model requires exchanging many datasets from the physical assets. Usually, it is performed on external servers within a cloud-computig architecture that communicates physical assets with the digital twin model. However, the cloud exchange introduces transmission delays and security and data privacy issues that hamper digital asset updates and create safety concerns. Hence, we propose an FPGA-based digital twin implementation where the datasets are taken directly from the physical asset running parallel to the digital asset. This setup eliminates the need for big data and cloud upload, ensuring data privacy and faster, efficient digital twin implementation and update. A case study is implemented to demonstrate embedded Digital Twin capabilities for monitoring mechatronic systems under fault events.  © 2023 IEEE.

title: Transnational Testing, Operation and Certification of Automated Driving Systems – Building bricks for the NATM multi-pillar framework
authors: J. Reckenzaun; R. Rott; O. Nikolić; P. Innerwinkler; M. Kirchengast; D. J. Ritter; S. Solmaz; S. Ladstätter; P. Luley; B. Toth; A. M. Hee; L. Hörmann; A. Pötsch; M. Rothacher; A. Rövid; Z. Vincze; M. Csonthó
source_title: 2024 IEEE International Automated Vehicle Validation Conference (IAVVC)
abstract: Pre-Sale validation, certification, homologation as well as after-sale monitoring, continuous (re-)homologation during operation of automated vehicles of all levels of automation are still posing major challenges to OEMS, suppliers, developers and certification bodies. These challenges are also reflected in current legislation and included in the latest assessment documents proposed by the UNECE (NATM). In this paper, we present building bricks for addressing these challenges. The building bricks originate from the current and final results of two European sister EUREKA projects. To handle complexity, specific driving functions (composed of the perceive-interpret-act cycle) for relevant operational domains and different perception pipelines were used as representative examples in the projects. As it is well known that the number of kilometres to be driven to thoroughly test the automated driving functionalities by far extends the feasible number. abstract: Immersive technologies such as Augmented Reality and artificial intelligence-based spatial computing may revolutionize the traditional pipeline mapping and visualization techniques. AR-based systems can leverage enhanced spatial awareness and better decisionmaking during excavation and construction activities through highly interactive and intuitive visualization of subsurface utilities. The AR-driven framework for high-precision underground pipeline mapping presented in this paper allows users to visualize water, gas, and sewer pipelines directly over the real world using mobile devices. The framework allows costeffective implementation with widely available smartphones, scalable deployment, and real-time interaction. Experimental data also revealed reduced dependence on specialized surveying equipment, enhanced user understanding, and more accurate visualization information. To sum up, a great opportunity exists for improving the dependability, efficiency, and safety of infrastructure management by adopting the proposed AR-based system for visualization along a pipeline. This method provides a feasible model for forthcoming smart cities and advanced spatial visualization systems for various applications.

The suggested framework equips project managers and government officials with a decision support system to allocate their budgets towards security measures that lead to sustainable results. title: Physics Informed Neural Operator for Battery Health Prediction and Lifecycle Management

abstract: To achieve safe, reliable and cost-effective lithium-ion battery operation, it is important to predict accurately the lithium-ion battery state of health (SOH) and the remaining useful life (RUL). Nonlinear electrochemical aging processes control battery degradation, and pure data-based models finds difficult to make accurate long-horizon predictions, whereas physics-based models can be computationally demanding and hard to tune across operating conditions. In this study, a Physics-Informed Neural Operator (PINO) architecture is introduced to predict battery health and lifecycle. This approach trains the operator mapping between battery utilisation history and SOH trajectories with a Fourier Neural Operator backbone and adds physical constraints that ensure monotonic capacity dissipation, charge throughput consistency, and end of life that are physically realistic. The validation is done using public run-to-failure battery data, and SOH is defined as $\text{SOH} = \mathrm{C} \_$ now/C_0, which is a popular formulation in battery health research. The suggested PINO has the best predictive performance with representative values of the RMSE (0.0080), MAE (0.0065), and MAPE (0.5) with superior physical consistency compared to the data-only models. The findings suggest that physics-informed operator learning is an effective approach to battery lifecycle management, digital twin building, and prognostic decision-making.

abstract: The construction sector has come up against some serious challenges for years, including inadequate production efficiency, enormous safety hazards, and a huge waste of resources on site. Existing research often concentrates solely on individual technologies and does not systematically integrate these technologies into a comprehensive solution, which limits the application of technology for the real-time monitoring and precise control of complex construction sites through traditional manual inspection processes. In contrast to this past research, the present research is based on the integration of digital twin, building information modelling, computer vision and IoT technologies to create an intelligent construction site monitoring system for building engineering, which enables a complete view of the construction site, and provides intelligent identification and precise controls over the entire site. This research is being conducted through the use of a four-layer structure that includes a “perception-transmission-platform-application” system. The first layer includes the “perception” elements, which consists of the collection of information from multiple sources using ultra-wideband positioning base stations, trained multi-media equipment (e.g. high-definition cameras), environmental sensors and drones; transmission of collected information is executed through a 5 G edge gateway; intelligent processing of the collected data is performed using YOLOv8 networks, SlowFast behaviour recognition networks, DeepLabV3+ semantic segmentation networks, with the use of Kalman filtering to combine the images and perception data; and, finally, the completed data is used at the application layer for visualized monitoring of the construction site, three levels of intelligent early warning detect, and 4D process management. Experimental results show that in terms of real-time performance, the system's overall average response latency is $\mathbf{8 5}$ milliseconds, a reduction of $\mathbf{3 3 5}$ milliseconds compared to the cloud architecture. Regarding recognition accuracy, the helmet wearing detection accuracy is 94.2 %, recall rate is 92.8 %, and $\text{mAP} {@} 0.5$ reaches 93.5 %, while the accuracy rate for normal work behavior recognition is $\mathbf{9 6. 4 \%}$. In data fusion, the root mean square error of personnel positioning is reduced to 0.35 meters, the tower crane status recognition accuracy is 91.3 %, and the false negative rate for abnormal events is 4.6 %. These research findings provide effective technical support and engineering application references for the digital transformation of China's construction industry.

abstract: Green intelligent buildings(GIBs) are a critical technological vehicle for achieving urban carbon neutrality, yet the dynamic interplay between technological synergies and sustainability objectives demands urgent interdisciplinary analysis. In response, the study proposes a multilevel resilience governance framework: a blockchain smart-contract-based dynamic carbon tax-subsidy model can enhance system-wide coordination effects, while participatory design can increase technology adoption. The resulting transparent decisionsupport system provides a quantifiable instrument to balance technological innovation potential, institutional effectiveness, and social equity; methodologically, the contribution lies in integrating dynamic game models with blockchain-enabled transparent governance, offering new quantitative support for technologyinstitution coordination.

Our novel Semantic Path Planning algorithm improves upon traditional grid mapping by using a multi-dimensional array in the map file, where varying intensities indicate occupancy levels. The planner imposes penalties on free cells near specific static objects based on user preferences, facilitating autonomous robot movement in designated areas without creating rigid barriers. A standout feature of our algorithm is its ability to prioritize specific zones frequented by vulnerable groups like the elderly, or areas designated for rest, pets, or children's play. Moreover, this methodology is promising for multi-robot systems with differing navigation abilities and access rights. It also improves robot localization by focusing on unique environmental landmarks, thereby enhancing tracking accuracy and aiding in swift localization recovery. This approach is ideal for safe, efficient, and context-aware navigation in dynamic shared human-robot environments.

abstract: In this work, we analyze the limits of parameter estimation of multipath components like their amplitude, delay and/or phase. Especially challenging is the estimation of such parameters when the multipath components have a low relative delay, i.e., less than half a tap delay with respect to the discrete channel impulse response. We will introduce the concept of the ambiguity subspace, which indicates that even for high signal to noise ratios and quite large RF bandwidths the Fischer information is limited and accurate estimation of the real world parameters becomes challenging. To overcome these theoretical limits, we propose the idea of ambiguity subspace resolution, ideally providing a solution close to the correct parameter values. There are a number of applications, which may benefit from the knowledge of the real world parameters like positioning, or, channel prediction. Here, we have in mind the building vector data map describing the environment of a digital twin of a mobile network, which is inferred from regular UE feedback of radio channel estimates. Such a digital twin is expected to support 6G use cases from optimized beam management, handover, load balancing up to channel estimation and/or channel prediction.

source_title: 2023 4th International Conference on Data Analytics for Business and Industry (ICDABI)
abstract: Blockchain technology has gained significant attention in the construction industry due to its potential to address critical challenges such as fragmentation, inefficiency, and a lack of stakeholder trust. Due to the growing research in this area, it has become essential to understand the evolving landscape comprehensively and identify the current state of research and future directions in the field of blockchain technology in construction. This paper aims to achieve this by conducting a bibliometrics analysis to map blockchain’s trends and research landscape in construction. The bibliometric analysis of scholarly articles and conference papers published in the Scopus database was used to identify the yearly trend of publications, influential authors, leading countries, prominent research institutions, and top journals in this field. Additionally, co-occurrence keywords were analyzed to explore the key themes and identify emerging trends and future research directions in blockchain-based construction. This study provides valuable insights for researchers, practitioners, and policymakers interested in understanding the current state and future prospects of blockchain technology in the construction industry. It also serves as a primary reference source for further studies in this area.

title: From IFC to GeoBIM Web Based CesiumJS Integration for Irrigation Asset Management
authors: Saptari A.Y.; Suhari K.T.; Widyastuti R.; Kusumawati M.; Saffanah H.
source_title: 2025 1st International Conference on Data Science and Geoinformatics, ICDSG 2025
abstract: Efficient irrigation infrastructure management is essential for achieving sustainable water distribution and agricultural productivity. This study presents the development of an Industry Foundation Classes (IFC)-based Building Information Modeling (BIM) framework integrated with CesiumJS to enable a web-based GeoBIM visualization system for the Pataruman Weir, Indonesia. Multi-sensor data acquisition—including Terrestrial Laser Scanning (TLS), UAV LiDAR, and handheld LiDAR—was conducted to achieve a geometrically accurate three-dimensional reconstruction, with a Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) of 0.032 m. The BIM model was semantically enriched according to the Ministry of Public Works and Housing Regulation No. 23/PRT/M/2015 and exported in IFC format to ensure OpenBIM interoperability. The model was then converted to 3D Tiles and deployed on CesiumJS for browser-based interaction. The resulting WebBIM system, named DAM2TWIN, integrates BIM semantics, spatial context, and Digital Terrain Models (DTMs) within a single platform, enabling visualization, spatial querying, and attribute inspection directly through the web. Performance evaluation demonstrated efficient rendering and data loading, validating the system’s capability to handle high-fidelity BIM models in lightweight web environments. This study highlights the potential of open GeoBIM workflows for improving transparency, interoperability, and data-driven decision-making in irrigation asset management, while providing a scalable foundation for future GeoAI and Internet of Things (IoT)-based digital twin applications. © 2025 IEEE.

title: Developing an IoT-Enabled National Cadastral Digital Twin Framework for an Integrated Geoinformatics Reference System in Indonesia
authors: Suhari K.T.; Purwanto H.; Sunaryo D.K.; Ariwibisono F.X.; Pradana A.H.; Saputri R.A.F.
source_title: 2025 1st International Conference on Data Science and Geoinformatics, ICDSG 2025
abstract: This paper presents the development of a Digital Twin framework for establishing a unified cadastral reference system in Indonesia. The research addresses persistent issues in the national cadastre, including data gaps, overlaps, and inconsistencies across institutions that arise from fragmented survey campaigns, heterogeneous mapping standards, and the absence of a unified, three-dimensional cadastral reference system capable of reconciling multi-agency datasets. At the international level, most existing Digital Twin implementations focus on infrastructure, mobility, or generic 3D city models rather than legally binding cadastre, leaving a gap in national-scale cadastral digital twins particularly in developing-country contexts. Integrating Building Information Modelling (BIM), Geographic Information Systems (GIS), and Internet of Things (IoT) technologies, the proposed system provides a three-dimensional (3D) digital representation of land parcels, ownership, and related assets. Data acquisition was carried out using oblique photogrammetry with a UAV Trinity Pro equipped with a D2M oblique camera system, achieving geometric accuracy with CE90 of 0.047 m and LE90 of 0.822 m. The prototype system, visualized through a WebGIS platform using CesiumJS, demonstrates how Digital Twin technology can support interoperability and multipurpose cadastral management. The IoT layer is implemented by linking cadastral objects in the 3D model to fixed CCTV camera sensors and their live metadata streams, allowing users to contextualize real-time observations within the cadastral Digital Twin. The study establishes a foundation for future GeoAI-based analytics in cadastral automation, spatial anomaly detection, and predictive land management toward a fully intelligent national cadastral system. In particular, the proposed National Cadastral Digital Twin (NCDT) prototype demonstrates how oblique multi-view 3D data, BIM–CityGML semantics, and 3D Tiles web streaming can be operationalized into a legally compliant and interoperable cadastral reference framework tailored to Indonesia, providing a concrete proof-of-concept for an IoT-enabled cadastral Digital Twin aligned with the One Map Policy. © 2025 IEEE.

title: A Multi-Sensor LiDAR–Photogrammetry Workflow for 3D Documentation of Sumbawa Besar Heritage Sites Toward H-BIM Development
authors: T. Satriawansyah; L. Mulyadi; A. U. Krismanto; L. K. D. Erlinda; K. T. Suhari
source_title: 2025 1st International Conference on Data Science and Geoinformatics (ICDSG)
abstract: High-fidelity 3D documentation of historic wooden architecture is essential for cultural heritage preservation and the development of Heritage Building Information Modeling (H-BIM). This study presents a multisensor Li-DAR–photogrammetry workflow applied to three major heritage sites in Sumbawa Besar: Bala Datu Ranga, Istana Dalam Loka, and Istana Bala Puti. Each monument was captured using tailored sensor configurations adapted to architectural scale, interior complexity, and accessibility, with accuracy validated through device-generated quality assessments. For Bala Datu Ranga, a hybrid GNSS–LiDAR–Visual SLAM system was used in PPK mode supported by terrestrial ground control points. The resulting point cloud achieved 100% compliance with the 5 cm precision threshold. More than 80% of the points fall within the 1–2 cm error range, and residuals on ground control points were on the order of 3–6 mm, demonstrating high geometric stability across both indoor and outdoor areas. For Istana Dalam Loka, a combination of static terrestrial laser scanning and handheld SLAM-based scanning was employed. Registration produced a global alignment error of 0.003 m, with individual cloud-to-cloud link errors ranging from 0.001 m to 0.007 m and overlap levels between 23% and 83%. These results confirm strong consistency between scanning positions throughout the building’s expansive multi-level wooden structure. For Istana Bala Puti, rapid indoor–outdoor mapping using a mobile LiDAR–SLAM platform yielded 100% of points within the 5 cm threshold. Approximately 24.5% of the points lie within 0–1 cm, 47.8% within 1–2 cm, and 27.7% within 2– 5 cm, indicating accuracy sufficient for architectural modeling and heritage-scale H-BIM development. Trajectory stability and GNSS quality metrics further demonstrate reliable performance in GNSS-degraded conditions through fused visual–LiDAR SLAM. In summary, the multisensor fusion of static TLS, handheld SLAM, PPK georeferencing, and photogrammetric texturing produced dense and accurate point clouds suitable for semantic segmentation, structural interpretation, and H-BIM generation. The results demonstrate that integrating multiple sensor modalities significantly enhances completeness, minimizes occlusions, and accelerates data acquisition for complex wooden heritage architecture.

title: Implementation of a Digital Twin Framework in the Modular Housing Industry
authors: A. Fischer; J. R. Llorens; Z. Cai; M. Wilke; S. Kessler; J. Fottner
source_title: 2022 IEEE 28th International Conference on Engineering, Technology and Innovation (ICE/ITMC) & 31st International Association For Management of Technology (IAMOT) Joint Conference
abstract: The construction industry is one of the minor digitized industries, and it has been characterized by a below- average increase in productivity in recent decades. The modular housing sector copies the production system of the manufacturing industry to meet these deficits, which makes it a perfect example for evaluating Industry 4.0 technologies. This paper explores the methodology and possibilities of implementing a digital twin of a modular housing production plant to optimize its production. The proposed approach based on a Digital Twin (DT) framework consists of three consecutive parts: (1) analyzing the production system by using the Lean tool of Value-Stream Mapping extended (x-VSM) towards Discrete-Event Simulation (DES) models, (2) collecting real- time data to track and trace the system's bottleneck by using Radio-Frequency Identification Devices (RFID) as a Tracking- and-Tracing system (TaT), and (3) optimizing it by using DES. Three scenarios to eliminate waste, increase throughput, and identify the best possible TaT implementation have been simulated. The results are a 64 % inventory reduction, a 20 % faster production lead time, and the finding of the critical part to be tracked using RFID. The resulting model has shown to be a valuable instrument for understanding the different process interdependencies. Moreover, it has been used as a support tool for middle management to assess the impact of different optimization approaches quantitatively. Overall, this paper shows the implications of combining DES and TaT systems towards a DT of a modular housing production plant.

title: Urban Mining: Applying Digital Twins for Sustainable Product Cascade Use
authors: A. Pehlken; S. Baumann
source_title: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Engineering, Technology and Innovation (ICE/ITMC)
abstract: Due to the ever-increasing consumption of resources, various materials and raw materials have become increasingly scarce and consequently expensive. At the same time, energy demand has dramatically increased in global mining operations also intensifying economic pressure. Surprisingly, the recapturing of important raw materials at the end of the product life cycle through recycling is still insufficiently implemented in the supply chain. Recycling is not only a sink for unwanted materials it can become an urban mine. This is especially relevant in Europe, where in comparison to other continents primary raw material mining of bulk materials is rather low. In a situation of scarcity, the exact planning of raw material and material flows for the following months (and sometimes years) has become ever more vital to ensure their timely and sufficient availability for production. A missing piece is the necessary transfer of production information (like bill of materials, BOM) to the recycler because information is typically kept inside the production supply chain. Digital technologies such as Digital Twins can help provide this information to the End-of-Life (EoL) stakeholders (recycling industry) as a means to increase the potential of circular economy. This paper establishes urban mining as an important concept of life cycle management in the circular economy. It uses a case study approach to explore the potential of urban mining for resource savings. The authors demonstrate that urban mining represents a high-impact application of sustainable engineering within life cycle management where Digital Twins help increase impact on sustainability.

title: A Conceptual Framework for AI-based Operational Digital Twin in Chemical Process Engineering
authors: E. Örs; R. Schmidt; M. Mighani; M. Shalaby
source_title: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Engineering, Technology and Innovation (ICE/ITMC)
abstract: As digitalization is becoming more and more an integral part of business in all sectors, the digital twin paradigm starts to play a more crucial role. This paper primarily aims at describing a generic framework for digital twin development in chemical process industry from an operational perspective. The main building blocks of the operational digital twin are presented, namely data management, process modeling, process optimization, production scheduling, and process control, as well as the deployment. Strong emphasis is put on the advanced process control hierarchy. Additionally, the role of artificial intelligence in the development and deployment of operational digital twin in process industry is presented, particularly regarding surrogate modeling, predictive modeling and AI supported optimization and control. Consequently the potential for new business models induced by digitalization is discussed, and an outlook for prospective research topics is provided.

abstract: Historic buildings, symbols of cultural heritage, represent unique architectural and cultural values. Historic buildings face the gradual erosion of materials and structures caused by time, climate change and the impact of human activity. Today, artificial intelligence (AI) technologies, including computer vision and deep learning, are opening up new possibilities in diagnosing, monitoring and planning the restoration of these historic monuments. This publication analyses existing AI applications in the restoration of historic buildings that allow detailed records and predictions of the condition of monuments, reducing the need for interventions that could compromise their historic integrity. Main focuses include automated damage detection, structural degradation analysis, and the creation of predictive models to support long-term maintenance. The article includes and/or analyses case studies that demonstrate the practical application of AI in architectural heritage conservation and discusses the benefits of implementing these technologies, including improved diagnostic accuracy and efficiency. The ethical and technical challenges associated with the application of AI are also analyzed, including costs, dependence on technology, and potential impact on authenticity. The results of this research contribute to the understanding of how AI can effectively support sustainable heritage conservation practices while respecting the historical value and aesthetics of the objects being restored.

abstract: The conservation and management of heritage buildings require comprehensive documentation and the integration of diverse information from multiple disciplines. Effective restoration and preservation efforts depend on the ability to conserve architectural, historical, and technical data within a unified digital environment. Heritage Building Information Modeling (HBIM) has emerged as a key methodology for collecting, organizing, and managing such data throughout the lifecycle of historic structures. This paper explores the application of the Scan-to-BIM process in the context of a historic mosque located in Al-Khabra, Al-Qassim, Saudi Arabia. By utilizing 3D laser scanning technology, the project captures highly detailed geometric data to support the development of a precise HBIM model. The study addresses the challenges encountered during the surveying and modeling phases, particularly in generating accurate parametric representations of complex architectural elements. The outcomes demonstrate both the potential and limitations of the Scan-to-BIM workflow in documenting Saudi architectural heritage and contribute valuable insights for future conservation efforts in the region.  © 2025 IEEE.

title: A Generalizable Design-to-Manufacturing Approach for Automated Timber Wall Construction
authors: Schulz D.; Bohm S.A.; Ris F.
source_title: International Conference on Electrical, Computer, Communications and Mechatronics Engineering, ICECCME 2025
abstract: Modern methods such as off-site construction, modular building, and robot-based manufacturing promise efficiency gains in the timber construction sector. This development is supported by concepts like Building Information Modelling (BIM), which integrates the entire building lifecycle. However, a persistent gap between design and construction phases remains insufficiently addressed by current approaches. As a result, processes are isolated and potential efficiencies are not fully realized. This work presents a Design-to-Manufacturing (DtM)based concept for automated production of timber walls. Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) are employed to analyze sheathing represented as point clouds, and to associate them with BIM data from the design phase. This enables extraction of process-relevant information, such as board and nail positions, directly from BIM data during manufacturing. Consequently, time-consuming steps like referencing with RFID tags or barcodes are eliminated, and boards no longer require sorting. For validation, a Digital Twin (DT) of a robotic cell and an open-source framework for generating point cloud data were established. In a comparative study of two popular GNNs, PointNet++ and DGCNN, analysis of boards using a custom, publicly available dataset of 10,000 point cloud models achieved F1 scores of up to 0.994 and IOU scores of up to 0.997 in semantic segmentation. These results provide a promising foundation for further developments in process integration in the field of wood construction.  © 2025 IEEE.

title: Advancements in Digitalization and Automation in the Construction Industry towards Sustainable Infrastructure: Present and Future Perspectives
authors: Anitha; A. B. Balulmath; R. Nayaka
source_title: 2024 IEEE Conference on Engineering Informatics (ICEI)
abstract: The construction industry is facing challenges in data management, quality, safety and decision-making due to its complexity and fragmented nature. Engineering informatics provides essential tools and methods to streamline the construction processes and enables data-driven decisions, enhances project quality and efficiency, supports sustainability development, and reduces project costs by integrating intelligent data processing into the construction lifecycle. The objective of this review article is to provide a comprehensive overview of the state-of-the-art in digitalization and automation in the construction industry, encompassing the various engineering informatics employed in the construction industry such as additive manufacturing in construction, building information modelling, internet of things, digital twin in construction, artificial intelligence, and machine learning. The present study utilized a systematic review methodology to thoroughly assess literature on digitalization and automation in the construction industry towards sustainability. title: Progressive Building Instance Segmentation on the Hessigheim 3D Photogrammetric Mesh Benchmark
authors: Zhou S.; Lu Y.
source_title: 2026 7th International Conference on Geology, Mapping and Remote Sensing, ICGMRS 2026
abstract: High-resolution triangular meshes generated from oblique aerial photogrammetry are increasingly used for 3D urban representation. While per-face semantic labels can now be obtained from established classifiers, these labels do not distinguish one building from another, a capability required by downstream tasks such as building-level energy simulation, LOD3 reconstruction, and digital-twin maintenance. Existing instance segmentation methods typically depend on deep learning and large annotated datasets. Most operate on point clouds rather than meshes, leaving mesh-native adjacency and surface-normal information unused. We investigate this problem on the Hessigheim 3D benchmark using all 18 validation tiles with 11-class semantic annotations, each carrying instance-level ground truth, covering 68 buildings in total. Building on a classical geometric pipeline of clustering, fixed-threshold region growing, and postprocessing, we propose two improvements: Progressive Region Growing (PRG), which replaces the fixed-threshold merge with a multi-round scheme under gradually relaxed normal-similarity and height-difference thresholds, and Boundary Regularisation (BR), which removes isolated noise, fills gaps via convex-hull analysis, and smooths instance boundaries. The combined pipeline raises the F1 score from 0.744 to 0.840, with precision improving from 0.618 to 0.841. Ablation experiments confirm that PRG and BR contribute complementary gains and that their combination outperforms either module in isolation. A texture-colour variant confirms that geometric cues dominate over radiometric ones on this dataset. The pipeline requires no training data and no GPU resources. © 2026 IEEE.

This method makes segmentation work better, even in tough urban settings like shadows, changing light, and dense building structures. abstract: The transition toward an urban circular economy (CE) is fundamentally a complex decision-making challenge characterized by highly heterogeneous data streams, fragmented policy landscapes, and conflicting stakeholder objectives. While Artificial Intelligence (AI) has emerged as a vital mechanism for data processing, existing research remains siloed within individual technical applications or localized sectors. To address this gap, this study conducts a narrative literature review with thematic synthesis to examine how AI comprehensively supports decision-making in urban CE transitions across three core dimensions: applied methodologies, operational sectors, and decision-making quality. The synthesis reveals a complementary division of labor where analytical methods (machine learning and predictive analytics) serve as cognitive engines, while physical systems (computer vision and AI-driven robotics) act as the operational executioners. Infrastructurally, AI interventions primarily stabilize the heavy-emission flows of the energy and waste management sectors, while emerging applications in the built environment, urban mobility, and bio-metabolic loops (water and agriculture) reshape spatial and resource circularity. Furthermore, this study establishes that AI elevates the caliber of governance from reactive crisis containment to an evidence-based, proactive paradigm. This is achieved by anchoring decisions in multi-criteria decision analysis (MCDA), predictive lifecycle design, and cyber-physical Digital Twins that automate regulatory compliance and simulate real-time scenario testing. Ultimately, this review offers a consolidated framework illustrating that successful urban circularity depends on integrating regional and urban planning with adaptive digital ecosystems, positioning intelligent decision support at the core of sustainable metropolitan governance. © 2026 IEEE.

abstract: During the operation of the key equipment of the space environment simulator, the equipment signals collected through sensors show non-stationary, small sample size and strong timing characteristics. The commonly used device health management methods are difficult to cope with such complex signals. The framework consists of a signal data segmentation layer, a data prediction layer, and an anomaly monitoring layer. The specific approach is to segment the signal sequences into sub-sequences using a sequence segmentation algorithm, and then identify each sub-sequence type using DNN. The subcooler pressure data are classified, identified, predicted and monitored using the proposed framework. The results show that the LSTM model can better predict the trend of anomalous data, and the Gaussian distribution model can provide early warning of potential anomalous data using the 3σ criterion. The classification accuracy of DNN model can reach 96.1% for small sequences, and the root mean square error (RMSE) of the LSTM model is 0.053.

abstract: Protection of endangered heritage objects or buildings is highly challenging and usually requires on-site visual inspection of experts to detect if any further intervention of a professional is required. Nevertheless, this type of inspection is time-consuming and not suitable for quantitative analysis. In this direction, 3D model analysis techniques have been proposed to detect 3D defects as an alternative to on-site inspections. In this work, we propose a coarse-to-fine defect detection approach. It includes an initial step for the data preparation, where all patches representing a neighbouring area of each point of the 3D structure are aligned (translated and rotated) to have the same orientation and the same ground point. Subsequently, a feature vector is estimated for each point used for an initial/coarse defect detection. Although most of the defects can be identified during this step, to improve our method further, we use a CNN-based learning approach, which receives the output of the previous step, to fine-tune the detecting accuracy. Evaluation studies using heritage 3D objects verify that the proposed approach provides promising results (74% accuracy for successfully detecting defects and 80% for detecting non-defects, respectively) to the automatic defect detection of 3D model surfaces.

abstract: With the deepening advancement of the Dual Carbon Goals (Carbon Peaking and Carbon Neutrality), precise accounting and responsibility allocation of carbon emissions in power systems have become core issues in the low-carbon transition of energy systems. Traditional macroscopic statistical methods and Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) methods struggle to characterize the spatiotemporal dynamic characteristics of carbon emissions accompanying the physical flow of electrical power, for which the Carbon Emission Flow Theory (CEFT) provides a novel analytical perspective. This paper systematically reviews the research progress on the coupling mechanism between electriccarbon flow and power flow both domestically and internationally, and comparatively analyzes the advantages and disadvantages of mainstream carbon flow tracing methods, including the Complex Power Tracing Method, Network Power Distribution Method, and Proportional Sharing Principle (PSP). Building upon this, the paper thoroughly explores the accounting boundaries of generation-side LCA Electric-Carbon Factors (ECFs), the emission characteristics across upstream/process/downstream stages, and the application of international benchmark databases (NREL, IEA). Addressing the challenge of multi-source heterogeneous data fusion, the paper elaborates on the construction technology of a spatiotemporal evolution model based on a Graph Database and Time-Series Database (TSDB), termed the 'Grid Single Map', encompassing automated ontology generation, nodal property graph fusion, and incremental topology inversion mechanisms. Furthermore, it systematically summarizes the calculation methodology for high spatiotemporal resolution ECFs, proposing a dynamic accounting framework that covers nodal-level carbon flow balance equations, network loss allocation mechanisms, and multi-level recursive aggregation from provincial to municipal to industrial park scales. Finally, the paper analyzes current challenges regarding data quality, algorithm real-time performance, and standard unification, while prospecting future directions such as electric-carbon market coupling, Digital Twin integration, and Artificial Intelligence empowerment, aiming to provide theoretical support and technical reference for refined carbon emission metering in power systems, green power trading pricing, and regional emission reduction policy formulation.  © 2026 IEEE.

abstract: This paper proposes a method to integrate the rich semantic data-set provided by Building Information Modeling (BIM) with robotics world models, taking as use case indoor semantic localization in a large university building. We convert a subset of semantic entities with associated geometry present in BIM models and represented in the Industry Foundation Classes (IFC) data format to a robot-specific world model representation. This representation is then stored in a spatial database from which the robot can query semantic objects in its immediate surroundings. abstract: The present paper proposes a lightweight framework for semantic segmentation of 3D point clouds of Indian temple architecture for digital heritage preservation and Heritage Building Information Modeling (HBIM). The proposed StructureAwareNet model combines spatial coordinates, surface normals, RGB information, and contextual architectural cues such as normalized height, centroid-based distance, and local point density to improve semantic understanding of temple structures. The results indicate that the inclusion of contextual structural features improves segmentation quality compared with geometry-based methods while preserving major architectural regions during prediction. The proposed model contains nearly 65,000 parameters and can operate efficiently in CPU-based environments without dedicated hardware acceleration. Overall, the framework provides an efficient pipeline for semantic interpretation and documentation of large-scale temple point clouds, supporting non-invasive and scalable preservation of Indian cultural heritage.

This study aims to explore these challenges through semi-structured interviews with four subject matter experts in the architecture, engineering, and construction (AEC) sector. Their insights shed light on the complexities of technology adoption, revealing not only established barriers but also emerging obstacles that have yet to be thoroughly investigated in existing literature. By identifying both recognized and novel challenges, this research seeks to provide a comprehensive understanding of the difficulties faced during the adoption of innovative technologies in construction. Furthermore, the study will propose targeted strategies to overcome these challenges, offering actionable recommendations tailored for organizations in the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) region. These findings aim to guide stakeholders in navigating the intricate landscape of technology adoption, ultimately fostering a more efficient and innovative construction environment.

title: Agentic AI in Optical Networks: Navigating the Autonomy and Abstraction Trade-offs
authors: M. Ahmadian; C. Natalino; P. Monti
source_title: 2026 26th International Conference on Transparent Optical Networks (ICTON)
abstract: Agentic AI systems — where large language models (LLMs) autonomously plan, reason, and act — are emerging as a compelling paradigm for managing the complexity of optical networks [1, 2]. Two independent design axes shape any such system. The first is autonomy: whether the LLM freely sequences tool calls and decides when to stop (ReAct-style open loop [3]), or whether control flow is pre-encoded as a deterministic graph, with the LLM invoked only at fixed decision points. The second is application programming interface (API) abstraction: whether the agent interacts with the network through semantic, domain-specific tools that encapsulate protocol details (high abstraction) or through raw protocol primitives that require the LLM to construct RESTCONF paths, resolve UUIDs, and parse nested YANG-model JSON directly (low abstraction). Note that high API abstraction reduces the LLM’s reasoning burden at the tool-call level, whereas low API abstraction demands greater in-context synthesis from the LLM — a distinction that is important when interpreting accuracy differences across LLM variants. Prior demonstrations over NETCONF/YANG [4] and OpenConfig [5] have shown the feasibility of LLM agents in optical network management, but none have characterized the architectural trade-offs that follow from these two choices. The gap matters: operators deploying agents on live infrastructure need to know which position in this design space best fits their requirements for generality, predictability, and trustworthiness. This paper makes two contributions. First, it establishes the autonomy × abstraction framework as basis for reasoning about agentic AI design choices in optical networking, covering all four quadrants of the design space. Second, it grounds the framework in three concrete implementations over the same T-API [6] digital twin: (i) a high-autonomy, high-abstraction ReAct agent with 18 domain-specific tools covering topology queries, optical performance monitoring (OPM), quality of transmission (QoT) analysis, and network (re)configuration across 12 scenarios; (ii) a low-autonomy, high-abstraction directed graph workflow that constrains the LLM to fixed invocations within a compiled agent graph with fully deterministic branching, including a modulation format cascade (DP-64QAM → DP-16QAM → DP-QPSK) executed without any LLM involvement; and (iii) a highautonomy, low-abstraction variant that replaces the 18 domain tools with 2 generic HTTP primitives, requiring the LLM to construct raw T-API RESTCONF paths, resolve UUID references, and navigate nested YANG-model JSON directly. The low-autonomy, low-abstraction quadrant — a directed graph calling raw protocol endpoints — exists conceptually but offers no practical advantage over the other three concrete implementations and is left as a boundary case. The three implementations are compared across five dimensions, three structural and two empirical. Generality: the high-autonomy ReAct agent handles all 12 scenario types covering topology queries, OPM, path analysis, lightpath provisioning, and multi-turn management; the directed graph handles lightpath provisioning only, evaluated across 100 randomly sampled node pairs from the CORONET CONUS topology. Predictability: every execution path of the directed graph is a deterministic function of typed state and fully enumerable at design time; the ReAct agents produce traces determined at inference time with unbounded tool-call sequences. Constraint enforcement: the directed graph embeds domain rules in branching logic the LLM never sees, enforced independently of model quality; both ReAct variants rely on the system prompt, making enforcement contingent on model compliance. Human oversight: the low-abstraction tools require the user to interpret low-level messages exchanged between the agent and the network controller, while the high-abstraction set of tools allow more precise human oversight due to each tool being linked to a specific functionality. Token cost: we measure how many tokens are necessary for each system realization to achieve a pre-defined set of goals as a representation of the cost to accomplish the tasks. Three key outcomes can be mentioned. High autonomy should be preferred when task diversity is high, and the full set of management scenarios cannot be anticipated at design time. Low autonomy should be preferred when predictability and auditability are safety requirements, or when domain constraints must be enforced independently of model behavior. On the abstraction axis, high API abstraction consistently reduces LLM error surface, prompt complexity, and operator evaluation burden; the engineering cost of building domain-specific tools is recovered in reliability and is progressively offset as interfaces such as T-API and model context protocol (MCP) standardize semantic operations at the protocol level.

title: Web Visualization Performance Optimization Techniques Using CityGML 3.0-Based Multi-LoD Generation and Hierarchical 3D Tiles Structures
authors: S. Park; S. Cho; J. Park; D. Jeong; E. You; I. Kim
source_title: 2026 Seventeenth International Conference on Ubiquitous and Future Networks (ICUFN)
abstract: This study proposes a Multi-LoD generation and hierarchical 3D Tiles conversion pipeline to address rendering performance degradation and network overhead issues in web-based 3D visualization of large-scale CityGML 3.0 datasets. Conventional approaches rely on a single LoD3 model, which results in continuous loading of high-resolution data regardless of camera distance, resulting in inefficient rendering. To overcome this limitation, LoD2 and LoD1 models are automatically generated using BIM-based attribute information in CityGML 3.0. The generated Multi-LoD datasets are then organized into a hierarchical 3D Tiles structure to support distance-based LoD switching. This approach enables selective loading of appropriate levels of detail according to viewing conditions, thereby improving rendering efficiency. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves approximately 37× faster rendering initialization than the conventional Single-LoD approach. Furthermore, reductions in the number of loaded tiles and memory usage, together with improved FPS during viewpoint transitions, were observed.

title: Integrating Energy System Monitoring and Maintenance Services into a BIM-Based Digital Twin
authors: Pruvost H.; Forns-Samso F.; Gnepper O.; Enge-Rosenblatt O.
source_title: IECON Proceedings (Industrial Electronics Conference)
abstract: The digitalization process is steadily increasing in the building industry and promises new perspectives for better designing and operating buildings throughout their life cycle. However, digitalization has not yet brought its greatest benefit for tackling the rising global energy demand and is even generally associated with more energy consumption. Instead, it has become urgent to rationalize energy use and decrease energy wastes. Indeed, buildings are responsible for about one third of the global energy consumption in the world [1], and 30% of this energy is even wasted through wrong or suboptimal operation, malfunctions and energy-unaware user behavior. Technologies supporting resource saving already exist for e.g. fault detection and mitigation, optimized energy systems control or predictive maintenance. But they necessitate much manual effort by experts to be configured and deployed since every building is to some extent unique with regard to its location, equipment and usage. Moreover, they require much expert knowledge and are not adapted for a daily usage by facility managers or even building users. These measures require also many data for continuous observation, analysis and system adaptations in real time. Although modern building management systems (BMS) can generate lots of monitoring data from sensors and meters, there is still poor or no reuse of building design data already produced in preliminary stages of the building life cycles. In view of these facts, this paper proposes a new data management workflow that relies on the reuse of building design information for facility management, and that shall fasten the deployment of energy-saving services while increasing user energy awareness and engagement in reducing energy use. For that purpose, this workflow makes use of building information modeling (BIM), knowledge graphs, data analysis and web technologies in order to develop a BIM-based Digital Twin for energy saving in the building operation phase. © 2023 IEEE.

title: RoofSam: Adapting the Segment Anything Model to Rooftop Classification in Aerial Images
authors: A. Bauer; J. -C. Krabbe; K. Kollek; J. Velten; A. Kummert
source_title: 2024 58th Asilomar Conference on Signals, Systems, and Computers
abstract: Foundation models, such as the Segment Anything Model (SAM), are transforming computer vision by enabling versatile architectures that can adapt to new tasks with minimal domain-specific data. In the geospatial context, however, these capabilities have been primarily examined for SAM's intended use case, image segmentation. This paper aims to extend SAM's capabilities beyond dense prediction by introducing RoofSAM, an adaptation of SAM specifically designed for roof shape classification in high-resolution aerial images guided by building outlines. RoofSAM utilizes SAM's interactive interface to effectively incorporate readily available prior knowledge about building locations through point-sampling processes. We evaluate several sampling strategies, including centroid and random sampling approaches, to determine their effectiveness in enhancing model accuracy. Our empirical and visual analyses demonstrate that RoofSAM can successfully transfer SAM's segmentation knowledge to the task of roof shape classification, achieving F1-scores of up to 86% for frequently represented classes, even with limited training data. These results underscore the versatility of vision foundation models in geospatial data processing applications.

title: Descriptor: Batteryless, Light- and Energy-Aware IoT Environmental Sensing Dataset (Li-IoT)

source_title: IEEE Data Descriptions
abstract: Research on low-power Internet of Things (IoT) systems has gained significant momentum within the broader context of green and sustainable IoT. In this setting, batteryless (BL) IoT has emerged as a promising solution to reduce maintenance costs and environmental impact by eliminating the need for battery replacements. As large-scale IoT deployments for monitoring and sensing applications continue to expand, important challenges arise in the design and operation of sustainable BL IoT networks, including long-term reliability, performance evaluation, and the analysis of energy-harvesting behavior under real-world conditions. To help address these challenges, this article presents a comprehensive dataset capturing the behavior of BL IoT devices deployed in an indoor environmental sensing network. The dataset comprises 100 days of measurements collected from sensors installed throughout an office building and includes data from two types of IoT devices: 1) plugged-in (PI) sensors with continuous power supply; and 2) BL sensors powered exclusively by energy harvested from indoor light. This dual-device deployment enables direct comparison of sensing performance, reliability, and energy dynamics between powered and energy-harvesting systems. The final dataset contains over three million samples collected from 28 sensors (14 PI and 14 BL) deployed across approximately 300 m${}^{2}$ of office space spanning nine rooms. The dataset provides a valuable resource for the systematic investigation of BL IoT systems, enabling rigorous analysis of deployment strategies, spatial–temporal sensing dynamics, energy-harvesting behaviors, system performance, and long-term sustainability considerations in next-generation self-powered IoT sensing networks. title: Key Industry 4.0 Technologies for Sustainable Built Environments: A Scope Review of Technology Integration and Its Impacts on Sustainability
authors: F. Machado; A. Amaral; N. Duarte; M. Araújo
source_title: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Industrial Engineering and Engineering Management (IEEM)
abstract: This paper systematically maps how digital transformation technologies associated with Industry 4.0 (I4.0) are conceptualised in relation to concerns within the built environment regarding sustainability. Employing a hybrid methodology that combines scoping review, bibliometric mapping, and thematic analysis, an initial corpus of 1513 documents from Web of Science and Scopus was refined to 83 influential peer-reviewed publications. The analysis identified thirteen key I4.0 technologies for sustainability in the built environment that are frequently discussed, including Building Information Modelling (BIM), Digital Twins (DT), Internet of Things (IoT), Blockchain, Artificial Intelligence (AI), and others, each demonstrating varying degrees of explicit sustainability relevance. Notably, the study uncovered recurrent combinations, or "technology stacks", such as BIM integrated with DT and IoT, or Blockchain combined with BIM and IoT, which significantly enhance sustainability outcomes through interoperability and functional synergies. Despite these findings, substantial conceptual fragmentation and inconsistent terminology were noted across the literature, limiting theoretical coherence and empirical validation. The study highlights the importance of standardised taxonomies and comprehensive empirical studies to rigorously validate technology stacks and their sustainability impacts across diverse built environment contexts.

abstract: The Shipengshan shipeng, a Neolithic-Bronze Age megalithic structure in Liaodong Peninsula, faces accelerated degradation from coastal weathering and human activities. This study evaluates the feasibility of 3D laser scanning for its digital conservation, aiming to (1) establish a digital twin framework for structural monitoring, (2) quantify crack propagation thresholds, and (3) validate virtual restoration protocols. Confronted with accelerated degradation due to coastal salinity, cryogenic weathering, and anthropogenic impacts, this study establishes an innovative digital conservation framework through 3D laser scanning applications. Our methodology integrates millimeter-level spatial documentation, non-invasive structural monitoring, and predictive conservation modeling, developing a tripartite system of “digital twin prototyping - risk prevention - augmented interpretation”. The results substantiate that shipeng's digital transformation enables high-fidelity preservation of eroding structural details through spectral reflectance capture, quantitative analysis of structural deformation vectors via time-series point cloud comparisons, and dynamic visualization of conservation scenarios through virtual simulation. This parametric conservation approach not only establishes a replicable model for East Asian megalithic heritage but also redefines value transmission pathways in the digital continuum.

abstract: Text-to-3D generation is a cornerstone technology for applications such as game development, virtual reality, and digital twins. authors: Ding C.; Ho I.W.-H.
source_title: IEEE Internet of Things Journal
abstract: Urban vehicular channel estimation (UVCE) has long been a difficult task due to the intercarrier interference (ICI) and path loss caused by high-speed vehicle motion and urban geographical features (e.g., buildings, vehicles, and trees). Conventional estimators based on pilot symbols and channel statistics generally assume static signal propagation models, such as Free-space and Rayleigh fading. These models are inadequate for addressing path losses caused by geographical features, leading to limited performance. In contrast, centralized learning (CL)-based estimators can provide higher estimation performance by collecting channel data from a specific geographical area for training. However, when the UVCE is scaled to city size, CL estimators cannot precisely recognize the channel characteristics of each location in the city, resulting in decreased estimation accuracy. To further improve the scalability and accuracy of UVCE, this article proposes a federated learning (FL) and convolutional neural network (CNN)-based channel estimator, referred to as FL-CNN. FL is used to aggregate multiple local channel models (LCMs), which are clustered by the K-Dimension (KD)-tree technique. For each LCM, we employ the ray-tracing model to calculate the path loss caused by geographical features and use CNN to estimate the channel. Our results show that at the low signal-to-noise-ratio (SNR) regime (e.g., 10 dB), the estimation and data recovery performance of the FL-CNN estimator are, respectively, 61% and 65% higher than those of benchmark estimators on average. © 2014 IEEE.
